title: Narrative layer: shared definitions
description: Definitions every piece of the narrative layer uses: how an item cites the text (support) and who may see it (visibility).

visibility.description: Who may see the item. `public`: may be published with the book and shown to readers by spoiler-safe features, gated by the item's reveal position. `author`: private to the author, never published. Absent means `author` (fail closed).

support.description: How an item is grounded in the text. Every assertion in the layer carries it.

basis.description: `asserted`: one cited paragraph states it (a time marker, a named place, a line of dialogue). `inferred`: it follows from reading, not from one sentence; `quote` is then required.

evidence.description: Paragraphs whose text supports the item. An address that does not exist in the manifest version invalidates the item.

quote.description: The literal words, copied from one of the evidence paragraphs, that justify the item. Required when `basis` is `inferred`.

confidence.description: Producer's confidence in the item, 0 to 1. Informative; consumers must not treat it as a calibrated probability.

status.description: Verification state: `verified`, `doubtful` (shown as such), `review` (needs a human). Absent means not verified.
